title: Porting the DID filter engine to JSON metadata added an Oracle branch that str.format()s user filter keys and values into a json_exists() expression wrapped in sqlalchemy text().

findings.explanation: The diff does not involve any SQL query construction or database interactions. The changes are purely data transformation (converting filter dictionaries to internal representations using InternalAccount and InternalScope constructors). No user input reaches a SQL query.

The list_dids_extended function accepts filters as a parameter, which now supports nested dictionary/array structures. The change allows filtering by 'account' and 'scope' fields. While the code converts these to InternalAccount/InternalScope, there is no visible ownership or authorization check to verify that the requesting user is permitted to filter by or view DIDs associated with arbitrary accounts or scopes. This could potentially allow a user to enumerate DIDs they shouldn't have access to by filtering on other users' accounts/scopes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add authorization checks to verify the requesting user is permitted to filter DIDs by the specified account and scope. Consider validating that the user owns or has explicit access to query the specified accounts/scopes before passing filters to the backend query.

findings.explanation: The client-side changes involve restructuring filter payloads and building URLs with parameters. The filters are passed to build_url() as a parameter dictionary. Date values are converted to strings via date_to_str(). This is client code that sends HTTP requests; SQL injection would occur on the server side if the backend constructs SQL unsafely. The client itself does not construct SQL queries.

The client code accepts a filters parameter and sends it to a remote API endpoint. Without visibility into the server-side implementation of the /dids/search_extended endpoint, it cannot be conclusively determined whether proper authorization checks exist there. The client-side change itself does not introduce authorization logic or bypass any checks.

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure the server-side endpoint /dids/search_extended validates that the authenticated user is authorized to query the specified filters (account, scope, etc.). Consider adding server-side authorization checks corresponding to the new filter capabilities.
